legacy_cells.B: Adversarial natural language processing: overview, challenges, and policy implications
legacy_cells.I: 028_2025_Adversarial natural language processing overview challenges and policy implications.pdf
legacy_cells.EN: Reviews adversarial NLP attacks and defenses; its practical example applies spelling errors, word splitting, and random perturbations. Healthcare is discussed as a policy context, not evaluated as a clinical application.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors describe a review integrating recent NLP attack and defense techniques, practical guidance and empirical comparisons, policy implications, and emerging methods such as Bayesian approaches.
legacy_cells.FN: The authors report that accuracy dropped by 30% under attack; Table 3 presents before/after attack accuracy and F1 for BiLSTM/CNN combinations on IMDB Movie and Twitter.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors acknowledge incomplete review coverage (some NLP synonyms were disregarded and preprints with fewer than 50 citations omitted) and a lack of standardized evaluation metrics and benchmarks.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors call for more resilient NLP models, hybrid defenses, and human-in-the-loop approaches to detect and mitigate adversarial threats.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify insufficient practical guidance, empirical comparisons of recent ensemble techniques, coverage of Bayesian methods, and overarching policy implications in prior reviews.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper is a broad adversarial-NLP review with a small text-classification attack example, not a healthcare world-model study. Healthcare appears in policy discussion; no clinical state, learned clinical transition, treatment-conditioned patient forecast, counterfactual comparison, or planning result is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FT: For robustness evaluation, report clean-versus-attacked metrics by model and dataset; this evidence does not establish clinical utility or state-transition validity.
legacy_cells.FX: Full extracted PDF text, pages 1–19. Specifically reviewed title/abstract (p. 1), introduction and stated gaps (pp. 2–3), literature review and attack/defense material (pp. 3–10), practical guidance and empirical Table 3 (p. 11), policy discussion (pp. 12–15), conclusion/limitations/future directions (p. 16), availability/declarations and cited prior version (pp. 17–19). Tables 1–2 were present but their extracted layouts were garbled; Table 3 was readable. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Tables 1–2 have garbled text extraction; no fields here rely on their specific entries. The paper states it extends Shaw et al. (2025), a HICSS proceedings paper, but the supplied metadata does not identify a paired local paper ID. Only B corrects a prefilled bibliographic value: the PDF title contains commas after “overview” and “challenges.” Evidence QA: 12/17 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (70.6%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 14 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 4 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All19 physical pages including complete references/end matter read; all pages rendered; Figures1–2 and Tables1–3 visually inspected (p4,6–11). No appendix included.
Own empirical example lacks split/sample counts/configurations/attack budgets/semantic-preservation checks; do not infer causal or clinical validity from classifier changes.
p10 calls procedure gradient-based, then describes random nlpaug attacks; source ambiguity unresolved. Wording accuracy dropped30% is retained as author wording, no conversion to relative change.
General Bayesian/calibrated uncertainty and human-in-loop benefits are recommendations, not demonstrated experiments in this benchmark. Cited works not independently retrieved.
Extends prior Shaw et al.2025 HICSS and references related BertGuard work; do not count as independent corroborating studies. Single-model source review, no human independent review/replication.
notes: Title page byline includes Mohammed Wasim Ansari, omitted in legacyC; raw cell retained. Taxonomy/survey contributions distinct from empirical Table3. Policy healthcare examples not evaluated clinical scope. Article CC BY/OpenData badge not evidence of code release or replicated performance.
